questions.definition: A person who starts and runs a business, taking risks to do so.
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs combine resources, make decisions, and accept the risk that the business may fail.

questions.definition: A person or group with an interest in the activities of a business.
questions.clue: Employees, customers, and owners are examples.
questions.explanation: Stakeholders can be affected by business decisions and may have different objectives.

questions.definition: The owners are not personally responsible for all business debts.
questions.explanation: Limited liability protects shareholders because they can only lose the amount they invested.

questions.definition: The movement of money into and out of a business over time.
questions.explanation: A profitable business can still fail if it runs out of cash to pay bills when they are due.

questions.definition: The income earned from selling goods or services.
questions.clue: Calculated as price multiplied by quantity sold.
questions.explanation: Revenue is not the same as profit because costs still need to be subtracted.

questions.definition: The amount left after total costs are subtracted from total revenue.
questions.explanation: Profit is a key objective for many private sector businesses and can be reinvested or paid to owners.

questions.definition: The level of output where total revenue equals total costs.
questions.clue: At this point there is no profit or loss.
questions.explanation: Break-even analysis helps businesses estimate the sales needed to cover all costs.

questions.definition: The process of collecting information about customers, competitors, and markets.
questions.explanation: Market research reduces risk by helping a business understand customer needs and demand.

questions.definition: The combination of product, price, place, and promotion used to market a product.
questions.explanation: A business adjusts the marketing mix to meet customer needs and compete effectively.

questions.definition: Cost advantages gained when a business grows and produces on a larger scale.
questions.explanation: Larger firms may reduce unit costs through bulk buying, specialist workers, or more efficient equipment.

questions.definition: The reasons why employees work hard and remain committed.
questions.explanation: Motivated workers may be more productive, have lower absenteeism, and provide better customer service.

questions.definition: The output produced per worker or per unit of input.
questions.clue: Higher output from the same resources improves this.
questions.explanation: Businesses try to improve productivity to reduce costs and increase competitiveness.
